title: Performance: Move regexp.MustCompile out of function bodies to package level
body:
### Description

In Go, `regexp.MustCompile` is an expensive operation that parses and compiles a regular expression. When placed inside a function body, the regex is recompiled every single time the function is called, which creates unnecessary CPU and memory overhead.

There are currently several places in the codebase where `regexp.MustCompile` is used inside functions instead of being declared as a package-level global variable. For example, in `libpod/oci_util.go` and `pkg/systemd/quadlet/unitdirs.go`.

I would like to help optimize this by hoisting these `regexp.MustCompile` calls to package-level variables so they are compiled exactly once at startup. 

Would the maintainers be open to a PR addressing this?
